author: Linnaeus, 1758
summary: 국내에서는 2002년 이후 흑산도·외연도·어청도 같은 서해 섬과 동해안의 삼척 등에서 몇 차례 기록된 길잃은새이다. 유럽에서 중앙아시아와 인도에 걸쳐 사람 사는 마을 둘레에 살며, 근래에는 중국 북동부까지 분포가 넓어졌다. 곡식과 풀씨, 곤충을 먹고 건물의 틈이나 구멍에 둥지를 튼다.

points.en: chestnut-brown sides of the head flanking the grey crown (male)
plain pale grey cheeks without a black spot (male)
distinct pale supercilium behind the eye (female)

sexes.male: 머리꼭대기가 회색이고 눈 뒤에서 뒷목까지 밤색이며, 뺨은 희고 멱에서 가슴까지 검은 턱받이 무늬가 있다.
sexes.female: 검은 무늬와 회색 머리꼭대기가 없는 수수한 갈색이고, 눈 뒤에 연한 담황색 눈썹선이 있다.

young: 암컷과 비슷하나 전체적으로 더 옅은 갈색이고 눈썹선이 흐릿하며, 부리가 연한 노란빛을 띤다. 수컷 어린새는 멱 가운데에 거무스름한 기가 도는 일이 많다.

similar.how: 참새는 암수가 같고 흰 뺨에 검은 반점이 있으나, 집참새 수컷은 머리꼭대기가 회색이고 뺨에 검은 반점이 없으며 암컷은 무늬 없는 갈색이다.

art.subject: House Sparrow (Passer domesticus), adult male in breeding plumage, a spring vagrant on a Korean offshore island: crown and centre of the nape grey; a broad chestnut band from behind the eye to the sides of the nape; lores and a small area around the eye black; cheeks and neck sides greyish-white; chin, throat and upper breast black, the bib widening onto the breast; mantle and scapulars chestnut-brown streaked black; rump grey-brown; wings brown with one bold white bar on the median coverts; underparts plain pale grey. Bill black in the breeding season; eye dark; legs pinkish-brown.
art.pose: hopping on bare ground among short weeds, side view
art.scene: weedy field edge and bare ground on a Korean offshore island during spring migration (May), bright light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding, side view hopping on the ground: grey crown, chestnut-brown sides of the head flanking the crown, plain pale grey cheeks with no black spot, extensive black bib, black bill, chestnut-brown back streaked black, pale grey underparts, pinkish-brown legs

adult female, side view on the ground: plain brown head without black or grey, distinct pale supercilium behind the eye, brownish-grey bill, brown back with darker streaks, no bib, pale grey-brown underparts
art.build: Small, stocky, big-headed sparrow, slightly larger and heavier than the Eurasian Tree Sparrow common in Korea; short neck and rounded body, hops on the ground. Bill stout and conical, shorter than the head, black in breeding males, horn-coloured in females and winter males. Legs short, pinkish-brown. Tail medium length, slightly notched, plain brown without white. In flight the white wing bar shows.
avoid: Do not paint a chestnut crown or a black cheek spot — those mark the Eurasian Tree Sparrow; the male House Sparrow has a grey crown and plain pale cheeks.
Do not shrink the black to a small chin spot; the breeding male's bib spreads onto the breast.
Do not paint a pale or yellow bill on a breeding male; it is black.
Do not streak the plain grey underparts.
